question: How Do I Add Custom Data to an Order That Isn't a Standard Field?
metaDescription: Order meta is the standard mechanism — a small snippet saves any custom key/value pair alongside the order, retrievable anywhere the order is loaded.
shortAnswer: WooCommerce orders support arbitrary custom meta data through the standard order object's meta methods, letting you attach any key/value pair (a gift message, an internal reference number, data from a custom checkout field) that isn't part of the standard order schema, and retrieve it anywhere the order is later loaded.

image.alt: Custom data attached to an order as meta, retrievable anywhere the order object is loaded later

bodyHtml:
How to Add and Retrieve Custom Order Meta

The order object's update_meta_data() and get_meta() methods provide the standard way to attach and read arbitrary custom data, and this is the same underlying mechanism a custom checkout field's value would typically be saved to when captured at checkout.

// Saving custom data to an order.
$order = wc_get_order( $order_id );
$order->update_meta_data( '_gift_message', $gift_message_value );
$order->save();

// Reading it back later.
$gift_message = $order->get_meta( '_gift_message' );

Things Worth Getting Right

  • A leading underscore in the meta key (like _gift_message) hides it from the default custom fields display in the classic order editor, which is usually desired for internal/system data rather than something meant to be manually visible/editable there.
  • Always call save() after update_meta_data(), since the change isn't persisted to the database until explicitly saved.
  • Displaying custom meta to the admin on the order screen (rather than leaving it invisible) needs a separate hook adding it to the order admin display, if that visibility is wanted.
  • HPOS compatibility is maintained automatically through these standard order object methods, since they're the correct, forward-compatible way to interact with order data regardless of the underlying storage system.

Implementing This Properly

  1. Use the order object's meta methods (update_meta_data()/get_meta()) rather than direct database queries, ensuring compatibility with both legacy and HPOS storage.
  2. Decide whether the data should be visible in admin and add appropriate display hooks if so.
  3. Test that the data persists and displays correctly everywhere the order is referenced (admin, emails, My Account, if relevant).

Need custom order data captured and displayed properly across your store? See custom WooCommerce development.
